cards.front: Recall a key point about Sedimentary Environments
cards.back: A sedimentary environment is a geographic setting where sediment is deposited, with characteristic processes and features

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sedimentary Environments
cards.back: Fluvial (river) environments: channels, floodplains, meanders; produce cross-bedded sandstones, laminated mudstones, channel structures

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sedimentary Environments
cards.back: Aeolian (wind) environments: deserts, dunes; produce well-sorted, cross-bedded sandstones (e.g. Old Red Sandstone)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sedimentary Environments
cards.back: Shallow marine environments: beaches, tidal flats, shelves; produce well-sorted sandstones, bioclastic limestones, ripple marks

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sedimentary Environments
cards.back: Deep marine environments: submarine fans, turbidites; produce graded bedding, greywackes, basinal mudstones

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sedimentary Environments
cards.back: Glacial environments: produce unsorted till (boulder clay), dropstones, striated pavements, varved clays

cards.front: What should you know about gcse geology exam tips — sedimentary environments?
cards.back: 1. For Sedimentary Environments questions, use correct geological terminology and classify features precisely 2. Reference specific geological time periods and processes 3.
